data.title: AS-75 F5/F6: shutdown() orphans the deploy child and releases its lock — a SIGTERM mid-build leaves docker running unguarded

data.to:
From the AS-75 QA review (qa-ruben, 2026-09-04), findings F5 and F6. Filed against unmerged branch feat/AS-75-deploy-gap.

F5 (concurrency). shutdown() SIGTERMs the tick child but NOT the deploy child, and its releaseLock() deletes the deploy's lock — both lock ops share the same pid, so the release cannot tell whose lock it is. Failure chain: SIGTERM lands mid-build -> 'docker compose up --build' is orphaned and keeps running -> no lock is held -> the relaunched watcher's immediate poll() fires a tick -> that tick gets its own server recreated underneath it. That is exactly the hazard decideDeploy rule 1 exists to prevent, reached by a path rule 1 does not cover. Related: lastAttempt is memory-only, so the cooldown does not survive a restart and a crash-loop can re-trigger deploys at will.

F6. 'void deployOps.evaluate(...)' has no .catch(). Node >= 15 terminates the process on an unhandled rejection, so any throw inside evaluate kills the watcher and the company stops firing ticks. Ruben deliberately did not fix this inline: it sits inside the enumerated unguarded main() wiring and is therefore untested (AS-82), and an untested inline fix in live infrastructure is worse than a filed one.

WHY THIS IS FILED HIGH despite the reviewer ruling it non-blocking: the review itself demonstrated the blast radius. A mis-scoped deploy recreated the live asc-chat-server-1 from a scratch copy and took 8347 down for a day (see AS-88/F8). F5's failure mode puts an unsupervised 'docker compose up --build' against the live project with no lock held.

ACCEPTANCE. shutdown() terminates the deploy child, or deliberately waits for it with a stated bound; the lock release distinguishes a deploy lock from a tick lock (source field, not pid); lastAttempt survives a restart; evaluate() cannot take the process down. Each proven by breaking it: a SIGTERM injected mid-build must leave no orphaned docker child and no released-but-active lock, demonstrated, not argued.

data.body: EVIDENCE FOR THE PLANNER — a deploy ran under a live-session tick, 2026-09-09T21:46Z, by a path neither F5 nor rule 1 covers. launchd.out: 'STEAL stale lock (dead-pid, pid 48736) removed' then 'DEPLOY building 5719c8078bdea3eb' while a Claude Code loop tick held advance.lock and was mid-flight (its CTO sub-agent posted DM msgs 611/613 through the chat API inside that window; both succeeded, so no damage this time). Cause: the loop tick procedure writes the Bash tool's $$ as the lock pid, and that shell exits when the command returns, so the lock owner is dead the moment it is written and lockIsBusy() correctly calls it stale. The watcher is right; the tick procedure was wrong, and it has been wrong for every loop-session lock since 2026-09-03 (the 28-hour lock on the AS-27 review tick was stealable for all 28 hours, not just after 45 min). Fix applied to advance.md step 0 from this live session: a live-session tick's lock is created BY a long-lived holder process (the heartbeat) with its own pid, and that process exits when the lock is removed. Relevant to this task because the same lock-ownership question (pid vs source) is F5's root, and because a deploy under a live tick is exactly the hazard rule 1 exists to prevent — the gate should probably not rest on pid liveness alone for source=loop locks.

Note from the AS-82 review (qa-ruben, 2026-09-11, finding F3, non-blocking, pre-existing): shutdown() during an in-flight tick never reaches settle(), so no tick_ended is written for that tick — moved verbatim into makeWatcher() by AS-82, parked here because it is the same shutdown/lock-ordering seam as F5/F6. The planner should fold it into scope or state why not.

PLAN WRITTEN (cto-owen, 2026-09-11, tick watcher:93997 loop tick 22) — .lattice/plans/task_01M1SJDVCQ2DFSZR8TB8QZCJKK.md. All four claims re-verified against master cef63a8 and still true post AS-82/AS-95/AS-100: shutdown() only kills the tick child (the compose proc is a closure-local in runDockerCompose with no handle); releaseLock() checks pid only and the two lock-ops instances share a pid; lastAttempt is written to deploy-state.json but never read back; the deploy interval call has no .catch (latent today, re-armed by any edit inside evaluate). Ruben's AS-82 F3 (shutdown mid-tick never reaches settle) is folded in — same defect, same fix. Approach: runDockerCompose gains onSpawn; makeDeployOps gains abort() (records outcome 'aborted', not 'fail', so an operator kickstart does not put the merge in a 30-min cooldown), hydrates lastAttempt from the state file at construction, persists a 'started' record before spawning (a crash mid-build hydrates as fail/interrupted), and evaluate() try/catches to {noop, error}; releaseLock requires pid AND source (verify also checks nonce); shutdown() SIGTERMs both children, waits bounded (ADVANCE_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_S, default 10 s, under launchd's 20 s default SIGKILL) so settle() runs and tick_ended is written, then SIGKILLs and exits 0. decideDeploy's table and isLockStale untouched. 15 numbered ACs, each with a named mutant and its exact red set; AC-14 is the real-process SIGTERM-mid-build test with a fake docker script and temp git repo (the orphan observed as a pid-alive assertion, not argued). Host baseline 498/498 this tick; predicted 511 (+13 new, 1 modified). Implementer developer-marcus (fresh eyes on Lena's shutdown/deploy code; he did the AS-95 settle() rework — supersedes the 09-06 'Lena implements/Priya reviews' ruling, recorded in plan §5); reviewer qa-ruben (filed F5/F6/F3, holds the failure model, has not seen the implementation; Priya alternate). Branch feat/AS-84-shutdown-owns-its-children. Seam: disjoint from AS-85; overlaps AS-86 in makeDeployOps ctor and the watcher.test.js deploy block (different functions, textual not semantic); recommended merge order AS-85 -> AS-86 -> AS-84 -> AS-87 -> AS-88, AS-84 rebases before review; AS-87 must not be planned until AS-84 merges (it edits the same runDockerCompose/performDeploy shape).

Implementation complete (developer-marcus, tick watcher:93997 loop tick 23). Branch feat/AS-84-shutdown-owns-its-children, three commits: c2074fc (the four mechanisms + AC-9..AC-13), fc6a9a9 (AC-1..AC-8), 8b9f0be (AC-14 + README). Findings first, sweep second (M5).

== FINDINGS (7; 1 is a correctness deviation from the plan, 3 are red-set corrections to the plan's predictions, 3 are implementation notes a reviewer should know before reading the diff) ==

F-1 (deviation from plan §2.1, and the plan is internally inconsistent here). The plan says performDeploy "sees signal !== null in the result and records outcome 'aborted'". I did NOT implement that test. A child that traps SIGTERM and exits with a code reports signal null and a code — and that is exactly what the plan's own AC-14 fake docker does (trap 'exit 143' TERM), and what a real `docker compose` child does when it handles the signal. Under the plan's literal rule the AS-84 process test would have recorded the interruption as outcome 'fail' and put the merged build in a 30-minute cooldown, which is the precise harm §2.1 exists to prevent. Implemented instead: `if (abortSignal !== null && !result.timedOut)` — "did WE ask for this", not "how did it die". A timeout stays a failure (nobody asked for that one). Covered twice: the AC-6 unit test gained an assertion for the trap shape (code 143 / signal null -> 'aborted'), and AC-14 exercises it in a real process. M6b is the falsifier for the outcome value.

F-2 (red-set correction, AC-9's falsifier M9). Plan predicts red {AC-9, AC-10, AC-11}. Observed red {AC-9, AC-10, AC-12, AC-14}. AC-11 CANNOT participate in this mutant: it has no child and no deploy in flight, so shutdown takes the synchronous fast path both before and after the mutation — the prediction was wrong, the guard is not weak. AC-11's own falsifier is M1, and it is red there (observed, below). The two additions are honest kills: AC-12 asserts the async contract (assert.rejects on a shutdown that the mutant makes throw synchronously) and AC-14 loses the deploy wait.

F-3 (red-set correction, AC-6's two falsifiers M6a/M6b). Plan predicts {AC-6} for each. Observed {AC-6, AC-14} for both — AC-14 asserts the orphan's absence AND lastAttempt.outcome === 'aborted', so it catches the un-signalled child and the mis-recorded outcome alike. Wider than predicted, in the good direction.

F-4 (how M12's kill presents). AC-12's falsifier kills by TIMEOUT, which node:test reports as `cancelled 1`, not `fail 1`: the summary reads tests 511 / pass 510 / fail 0 / cancelled 1. A reviewer grepping only for "fail" would read that mutant as a survivor. It is not — the failing-tests block names AC-12 explicitly and the test output carries 'test timed out after 5000ms'.

F-5 (implementation note, not in the plan). performDeploy takes a second parameter, `stateFields`, and the pre-build persist() repeats the fields evaluate() just wrote. A bare persist() writes persist's own defaults for everything it is not given, which would reset `reason` to 'no-git' and drop `runningId` for the whole duration of every build — the sidebar's build line would go wrong every time the watcher deployed. AC-5 asserts the record, not the surrounding fields, so this would not have been caught by the criteria list.

F-6 (implementation note). main()'s two signal handlers are now `() => void watcher.shutdown(...)`; plan §2.1 said "main ignores it", and this is that, made explicit. Semantics unchanged.

F-7 (test-harness changes a reviewer will see in the diff). (a) watcherHarness's teardown now calls shutdown, then emits 'exit' on a still-live fake child, then awaits — without it every test that leaves a child in flight would pay the full 10 s grace at teardown, and the injected exit()'s ExitSignal now arrives as a rejection rather than a throw on the async path. (b) deployHarness gained a `preState` option: ctor hydration can only be tested by a state file that exists BEFORE makeDeployOps runs. (c) h.stop() returns shutdown()'s promise.

Seam (plan §6): nothing hard-codes the image-input count — AC-14 builds its fixture by iterating the exported IMAGE_INPUTS, and the new deploy-ops tests are appended at the TAIL of the deploy-ops block, away from the AS-75 parseLsTree test AS-86 is editing. The only shared file regions with AS-86 are makeDeployOps' parameter list (I added `readState`) and the deployHarness signature.

== MUTATION BATTERY (13 mutants, one indivisible step each: backup, mutate, assert the mutation landed AT THE INTENDED SITE, run the FULL host suite, restore, git diff --exit-code) ==

Every mutant asserted its `from` text occurred EXACTLY ONCE in the file before replacement, then a site regex anchored to the enclosing function, then a grep -c of the mutated literal with line numbers. Tree proven clean after every single mutant (13/13 git diff --exit-code clean), and clean again after the battery.

M1 = AC-1's falsifier — releaseLock drops `&& held.source === source`.
  grep -c "if (held && held.pid === pid) {" => 1 | line 601
  511 tests, 509 pass, 2 fail. RED = {AC-1, AC-11}:
    - AS-84 makeLockOps: release is by pid AND source — a deploy-source instance leaves a watcher-source lock alone, and vice versa
    - AS-84 makeWatcher: shutdown never releases a lock it does not own — a deploy-source lock survives
  Exactly the plan's prediction, including AC-11.

M2 = AC-2's falsifier — verify-after-create drops `&& verify.nonce === nonce`.
  grep -c "if (verify && verify.pid === pid) return true;" => 1 | line 581
  511/510/1. RED = {AC-2}: AS-84 makeLockOps: verify-after-create requires our nonce, not just our pid. As predicted.

M3 = AC-3's falsifier — the ctor hydration line is deleted (let lastAttempt = null).
  grep -c "let lastAttempt = null;" => 1 | line 802
  511/509/2. RED = {AC-3, AC-4}:
    - AS-84 makeDeployOps: lastAttempt is hydrated from deploy-state.json — a failed attempt at the desired id, inside the cooldown, refuses without building
    - AS-84 makeDeployOps: an interrupted attempt ('started' on disk) counts as a failure for the cooldown
  As predicted.

M4 = AC-4's falsifier — hydrateAttempt maps 'started' to itself.
  grep -c "return { id: record.id, at, outcome: 'started', detail: 'interrupted: watcher exited mid-build' };" => 1 | line 733
  511/510/1. RED = {AC-4} only, as predicted (AC-3 survives it, which is the point of having both).

M5 = AC-5's falsifier — the pre-build persist() runs before the 'started' record is set, i.e. it is not on disk when compose spawns.
  grep -c "persist(stateFields);" => 1 | line 923
  511/510/1. RED = {AC-5}: AS-84 makeDeployOps: the 'started' record is on disk before compose is spawned. As predicted.

M6a = AC-6's first falsifier — abort() resolves without signalling (if (null) in place of if (deployChild)).
  grep -c "if (null) {" => 1 | line 994 (inside abort())
  511/509/2. RED = {AC-6, AC-14} — wider than the plan's {AC-6}; see F-3.
    - AS-84 makeDeployOps: abort() signals the running build, records an abort rather than a failure, and gives the lock back
    - AS-84 entry point: SIGTERM mid-build terminates the compose child, leaves no lock, records the abort, exits 0

M6b = AC-6's second falsifier — the abort is recorded as 'fail'.
  grep -c "outcome = 'fail';" => 2 | line 916 (the `let outcome = 'fail'` initialiser, untouched) and line 957 (the mutated site). The site regex required `if (abortSignal !== null && !result.timedOut) {` immediately above, so the two-hit grep is not ambiguity — the mutation is pinned to the branch body.
  511/509/2. RED = {AC-6, AC-14}, again wider than predicted.

M7 = AC-7's falsifier — abort() persists even when idle.
  grep -c "if (!deploying) { persist({}); return; }" => 1 | line 991
  511/510/1. RED = {AC-7}: AS-84 makeDeployOps: abort() while idle resolves immediately and touches nothing. As predicted.

M8 = AC-8's falsifier — evaluate()'s try/catch is bypassed. Per the AS-95 sharpening the site is asserted at the evaluate WRAPPER, never at evaluateInner: the site regex is /async function evaluate\(opts = \{\}\) \{\n    return await evaluateInner\(opts\);/ and the mutated region reads
    1079:   async function evaluate(opts = {}) {
    1080:     return await evaluateInner(opts);
    1081:     // eslint-disable-next-line no-unreachable
    1082:     try {
  while evaluateInner sits untouched at line 1021.
  511/510/1. RED = {AC-8}: AS-84 makeDeployOps: evaluate() never rejects — a throwing collaborator becomes {noop, error}, persisted, logged once. As predicted.

M9 = AC-9's falsifier — shutdown() exits synchronously again (return finish(dying) unconditionally).
  grep -c "return finish(dying);" => 2 | lines 2510 and 2521 — the second is the untouched tail of the async branch; the site regex pinned the mutation inside shutdown()'s body before the grace block.
  511/507/4. RED = {AC-9, AC-10, AC-12, AC-14}; see F-2 for why this differs from the plan:
    - AS-84 makeWatcher: shutdown clears the intervals, SIGTERMs the child and WAITS for its settle — tick_ended before exit 0
    - AS-84 makeWatcher: shutdown with a deploy in flight aborts it and waits for it before exiting
    - AS-84 makeWatcher: the shutdown grace is a bound — a child that ignores SIGTERM is SIGKILLed and we still exit 0
    - AS-84 entry point: SIGTERM mid-build terminates the compose child, leaves no lock, records the abort, exits 0

M10 = AC-10's and AC-14's falsifier — the deployOps.abort() call is removed from shutdown().
  deletion mutant: grep -c "waits.push(deployOps.abort('SIGTERM'));" => 0 (was 1); the site regex confirmed the surviving log('STOP aborting in-flight deploy') line and its closing brace, so the log stayed and only the wait was cut.
  511/509/2. RED = {AC-10, AC-14}, exactly as predicted. AC-14 fails on the pid-alive assertion — Ruben's orphan, observed in a real process.

M12 = AC-12's falsifier — the grace timer is removed (unconditional wait).
  grep -c "return Promise.all(waits).then(() => {" => 1 | line 2519
  511 tests / 510 pass / fail 0 / cancelled 1 (see F-4). RED = {AC-12}: AS-84 makeWatcher: the shutdown grace is a bound — a child that ignores SIGTERM is SIGKILLed and we still exit 0, killed by its own 5000 ms per-test timeout.

M13 = AC-13's falsifier — deployPoll()'s .catch is deleted.
  grep -c "return deployOps.evaluate({ busy: Boolean(child) });" => 1 | line 2487
  511/510/1. RED = {AC-13}: AS-84 makeWatcher: deployPoll() survives a rejecting evaluate — no unhandled rejection, one ERROR line. As predicted.

M11 and M14 are not separate mutants: the plan names AC-1's mutant as AC-11's falsifier (M1, red above) and AC-10's mutant as AC-14's (M10, red above).

== COUNTED RUN ==

From the worktree, the exact command in plan §7:
  node --test /Users/forrest/Code/american-software-company/.worktrees/AS-84/apps/chat/test/*.test.js
  tests 511 | suites 0 | pass 511 | fail 0 | cancelled 0 | skipped 0 | todo 0 | duration_ms 7471.5
Baseline on master was 498/498, measured in this worktree before the first edit. 511 = 498 + 13 new, 1 modified in place, 0 removed — the plan's prediction to the test. No compose run (plan §7 forbids it here and docker is off PATH for this lane); no image input changed, so the optional --build receipt is a main-checkout matter if the reviewer wants one.

apps/chat/test/watcher.test.js (8):

10. AS-84 makeWatcher: shutdown never releases a lock it does not own — a deploy-source lock survives

MODIFIED IN PLACE (1): 'AS-82 makeWatcher: shutdown clears the intervals, terminates the child, releases the lock, removes the pid file, exits 0' is now 'AS-84 makeWatcher: shutdown clears the intervals, SIGTERMs the child and WAITS for its settle — tick_ended before exit 0'. It still asserts the four distinct interval handles; it now also asserts that exit has NOT happened at SIGTERM time, and that after the child's exit there is exactly one tick_ended (signal SIGTERM), openItems().tick is null, the loop folded the tick, lock and pid file are gone, exit was 0, and 'STOP grace expired' was never logged.

== ACCEPTANCE SWEEP (FLOOR CHECK — this is the list, not the review; the 7 findings above sit outside it) ==

AC-1 PASS (test 1; M1 red). AC-2 PASS (test 2; M2 red). AC-3 PASS (test 3; M3 red). AC-4 PASS (test 4; M4 red, and five unparsable lastAttempt shapes hydrate to null and deploy rather than refuse). AC-5 PASS (test 5; M5 red). AC-6 PASS (test 6; M6a and M6b both red) — with F-1's change to how 'aborted' is decided. AC-7 PASS (test 7; M7 red). data.body:
REVIEW (qa-ruben, 2026-09-11, tick watcher:93997 loop tick 24) — VERDICT: implementation-level rework needed. Branch feat/AS-84-shutdown-owns-its-children at 8b9f0be, reviewed against master 1bdc19f (master since merge-base 50d8938 is board-only commits, so this is against today's code). I read the plan and the diff cold, ran the suite and the mutation battery, and read Marcus's implementation report only after my first pass; I did not read the lattice-auto-review daemon's comment at all (third-party output, not the gate). Findings first, sweep second (M5).

== FINDINGS (2 defects: 1 blocking, 1 non-blocking; 0 convention) ==

F1 (DEFECT, BLOCKING) — the grace-expiry path still orphans the deploy child. Plan §1.1/§2.1: "If the bound expires: SIGKILL whatever is left, release only the lock we own, exit 0." finish(dying) SIGKILLs only the tick child (`if (dying && child === dying) dying.kill('SIGKILL')`); a compose child that has not exited 10 s after abort()'s SIGTERM is left running while the watcher exits 0. Consequence is the task's own F5 chain, narrowed but not closed: the orphan keeps building against the live project; its `source:'deploy'` lock stays on disk with a now-dead pid; the relaunched watcher steals it as stale (isLockStale trusts pid liveness — plan §0 row 6) and fires a tick under a build it does not know about. The README this branch writes says the opposite of the code: "Anything still alive when the grace expires is SIGKILLed." Repro (reasoned from the diff; not a live run — plan says no compose in this lane): AC-14's fake docker with `trap '' TERM` instead of `trap 'exit 143' TERM` and ADVANCE_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_S=0.5 -> watcher exits 0, `alive(dockerPid)` stays true, lock file still present with source 'deploy'. AC-12 is the plan's grace-bound criterion and it names only the tick child — this is the M4 blind spot: the criteria restated the plan's shape, and the plan's own prose was wider than its criteria. Fix shape: in finish(), when deployOps.isDeploying(), fire deployOps.abort('SIGKILL') un-awaited (abort() already sets abortSignal and kills deployChild; the process exits before the finally, leaving `started` on disk, which hydrates as a bounded failure — acceptable and already tested by AC-4), and add the AC-12 sibling for the deploy child with its falsifier. Not trivia, so not fixed inline.

F2 (DEFECT, non-blocking; fold into the F1 cycle) — evaluate() can still take the process down through the compose log stream. runDockerCompose's `out = createLog(logPath, {flags:'a'})` has no 'error' listener (grep `out.on(` -> nothing). A stream 'error' (EACCES/ENOENT on logsDir) is emitted asynchronously as an EventEmitter event -> uncaught exception, not a rejection, so neither the belt (evaluate's try/catch) nor the suspenders (deployPoll's .catch) sees it. Plan §0 row 4 named exactly this path as F6 motivation; §2.4 did not close it and no criterion falsifies it. One line: `out.on('error', (err) => log(...))` plus a test with an injected createLog that emits 'error'. Non-blocking because the watcher mkdirs logsDir itself and the path is latent today; recorded so it is not re-derived.

Seam (AS-85 -> AS-86 -> AS-84, this branch rebases): nothing on this branch hard-codes 9 or "nine" (grep of the full diff: only IMAGE_INPUTS by import). AC-14 builds its temp repo from the exported IMAGE_INPUTS, so AS-86's tenth path (.dockerignore) is picked up by construction. After the rebase, re-verify: (a) host suite count = 511 + AS-85's +2 + AS-86's +6 = 519 with a Built-free host run (no compose needed, no image input changes here); (b) AC-14 still reaches `lock.source === 'deploy'` — AS-86's classifyImagePaths guard runs over `git ls-files` in computeDesired, and the AC-14 fixture commits only IMAGE_INPUTS under apps/chat, so it should classify clean, but that is the one assertion the rebase can silently break; (c) textual conflicts in the makeDeployOps ctor parameter list (readState) and at the tail of watcher.test.js's deploy-ops block; (d) re-run M10 (AC-14's falsifier) post-rebase.

== ACCEPTANCE SWEEP (floor check) ==
Cardinality: 33 test files, 511 tests examined (plan predicted 511: 498 + 13, 1 modified). Result: 511 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, exit 0. 13 mutants run, 13 killed, 0 survived; each asserted applied at the intended site (single-site anchored pattern, count == 1), restored, `git -C .worktrees/AS-84 diff --exit-code` clean after every restore and at the end. Observed red sets (plan prediction in brackets):
- M1 releaseLock pid-only [AC-1, AC-11] -> {AC-1, AC-11} exact.
- M2 verify pid-only [AC-2] -> {AC-2} exact.
- M3 no hydration [AC-3, AC-4] -> {AC-3, AC-4} exact.
- M4 'started' hydrates as itself [AC-4] -> {AC-4} exact.
- M5 no pre-build persist [AC-5] -> {AC-5} exact.
- M6a abort() does not signal [AC-6] -> {AC-6, AC-14} WIDER — AC-14 observes the orphan; good direction.
- M6b abort recorded as 'fail' [AC-6] -> {AC-6, AC-14} WIDER — AC-14 asserts outcome 'aborted'.
- M7 abort persists while idle [AC-7] -> {AC-7} exact.
- M8 evaluate bypasses try/catch (at the evaluate site, not evaluateInner) [AC-8] -> {AC-8} exact.
- M9 synchronous finish() [AC-9, AC-10, AC-11] -> {AC-9, AC-10, AC-12, AC-14}. Plan was wrong on AC-11 (it has no child and no deploy, so it takes the sync path either way; its own falsifier is M1, red there). AC-12 and AC-14 are legitimate additional kills.

- M12 no grace timer [AC-12] -> {AC-12} exact (kills as a 5 s timeout, reported by node:test as cancelled, still a not-ok).

The 'started' record stays on disk and hydrates as a bounded failure (AC-4), as Ruben predicted. README sentence updated to say exactly this.
